newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds higher on interbank.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds higher on interbank.

text.p: Singapore government bonds closed higher across the board on moderate interbank and retail interest following a softer interbank rate, dealers said on Monday.
"Bond prices were marked up slightly today as the interbank eased slightly towards the close. Treasury bills were slightly easier and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.68/2.63 percent compared with last Friday's yield of 2.82/2.77 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.65/2.60 percent against 2.70/2.65 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.58/98.63 from last Friday's close of S$98.54/98.59, September 2001 at S$96.45/96.55 versus S$96.20/96.25 and June 2003 at S$94.43/94.48 against S$94.32/94.37.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 2-7/8 2-3/4 percent from last Friday's 3 2-7/8 percent.
